sentences.en: The task force is just – it's a 10-week campaign all in all.
sentences.zh: 特遣舰队只是——总而言之，这是一场为期10周的战役。

sentences.en: But for most of that time, the task force is just kind of plowing through the waves.
sentences.zh: 但在大部分时间里，特遣舰队只是在海浪中破浪前行。

sentences.en: So it's a bit like a test match.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像板球对抗赛。

sentences.en: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Long periods and then sudden explosive action.
sentences.zh: 漫长的相持期，然后是突然爆发的行动。

sentences.en: Well, except there's no action at all to start with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了刚开始时根本没有任何行动。

sentences.en: Because basically, all that's happening is these blokes are on the ships, sunbathing, and they're just sort of limbering up.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，所有发生的事情就是这些家伙在船上晒日光浴，他们只是在做热身准备。

sentences.en: But it all doesn't – at that point, it doesn't really seem real.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，这一切看起来并不那么真实。

sentences.en: So a lot of the soldiers are saying, well, you know, it'll be actually going to be fighting.
sentences.zh: 所以很多士兵都在说，好吧，你知道，我们真的要打仗吗？

sentences.en: Will we get back in time for the World Cup, which is happening in Spain that summer?
sentences.zh: 我们能赶回国去看今年夏天在西班牙举行的世界杯吗？

sentences.en: But Dominic, one thing that does happen is we mentioned South Georgia in the first episode.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，确实发生了一件事，我们在第一集里提到过南乔治亚岛。

sentences.en: Scrap metal.
sentences.zh: 废金属。

sentences.en: The scrap metal behaved disgracefully by barbecuing a reindeer.
sentences.zh: 那些废金属通过烤驯鹿做出了极其恶劣的举动。

sentences.en: And this is the first clash between British and Argentine forces, and it's a total British victory, right?
sentences.zh: 而这也是英阿两军之间的首次交锋，而且这是一场彻头彻尾的英国胜利，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, although it's a bit more traumatic than that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过情况比那要痛苦得多，汤姆。

sentences.en: Because a few helicopters go blown up and things.
sentences.zh: 因为有几架直升机被炸毁之类的。

sentences.en: So I think I said before, the 16th of April, the first aircraft carriers got to Ascension Island.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我之前说过，4月16日，第一艘航空母舰到达了阿森松岛。

sentences.en: And at that point, there are 127 ships in the fleet.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，舰队里有127艘船。

sentences.en: So it's a bloody big fleet, and there's about 10,000 men.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一支规模庞大的舰队，大约有一万名官兵。

sentences.en: And when they get to Ascension Island, they divide off 150 Royal Marines and 70 men from the SAS,
sentences.zh: 当他们到达阿森松岛时，他们分出了150名皇家海军陆战队员和70名特种空勤团士兵，

sentences.en: and they're basically going to go off to South Georgia, which is, you know, as we said before, hundreds of miles away from the Falkland Islands.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上要前往南乔治亚岛，正如我们之前所说，该岛距离福克兰群岛有数百英里远。

sentences.en: It's really important that the government gets an early victory.
sentences.zh: 政府取得一个早期胜利非常重要。

sentences.en: But South Georgia, you know, it's practically – you're virtually in Antarctica, where you're getting on the way to Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 但南乔治亚岛，你知道的，实际上——你基本上就在南极洲，或者说是在去往南极洲的路上。

sentences.en: So when the first helicopters go, 21st of April, they drop these blokes.
sentences.zh: 所以当第一批直升机在4月21日出发时，他们把这些家伙投送了下去。

sentences.en: They're on a glacier.
sentences.zh: 他们在冰川上。

sentences.en: The tents blow away.
sentences.zh: 帐篷被风吹走了。

sentences.en: It's kind of Shackleton, the terror style kind of freezing.
sentences.zh: 这有点像沙克尔顿那种极地惊悚风格的严寒。

sentences.en: Yes, monsters lurching up out of holes in the grime.
sentences.zh: 没错，怪物从冰雪的洞穴里蹒跚而出。

sentences.en: Basically, most of the tents are blown away.
sentences.zh: 基本上，大部分帐篷都被吹走了。

sentences.en: There's got about a couple of tents left, and they're all – some of the men are in the tents, and the other men are trying to shovel snow away, and it's just awful.
sentences.zh: 只剩下两顶左右的帐篷了，他们全都在——有些人在帐篷里，其他人则在拼命铲雪，情况简直糟透了。

sentences.en: And they basically have to radio and say, come and get us.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上不得不通过无线电呼叫，说，快来接我们吧。

sentences.en: This isn't going to work at all.
sentences.zh: 这根本行不通。

sentences.en: The helicopters then crash.
sentences.zh: 接着直升机坠毁了。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher gets the news the helicopters crash, and she thinks the men are dead.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人听到直升机坠毁的消息，以为士兵们都遇难了。

sentences.en: So she bursts into – you know, she starts crying.
sentences.zh: 所以她突然情绪失控——你知道的，她开始哭泣。

sentences.en: It's the first moment of casual – it's the first operation, really, of the war, and it's all gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是战争中真正意义上的第一次人员伤亡——也是第一次军事行动，结果却一团糟。

sentences.en: And then she gets the news that a third helicopter has got there and got them out, and she's absolutely on cloud nine.
sentences.zh: 然后她得到消息，第三架直升机赶到并把他们救了出来，她顿时高兴得飘飘然。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a real psychological turning point for her because that really emboldens her.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对她来说是一个真正的心理转折点，因为这极大地鼓舞了她。

sentences.en: In future, she's going to be much less keen on peace.
sentences.zh: 此后，她对和平的兴趣将大打折扣。

sentences.en: She starts to identify with the men, and they're slightly sort of –
sentences.zh: 她开始认同这些士兵，他们有点像是——

sentences.en: Our boys.
sentences.zh: 我们的男孩。

sentences.en: Yeah, our boys, our brave boys, our lads, all that sort of stuff from that point onwards.
sentences.zh: 对，我们的男孩，我们勇敢的男孩，我们的小伙子们，从那以后全都是这套说辞。

sentences.en: Then on the 25th, which is a Sunday, Mrs. Thatcher's at Chequers, and she gets the news that they're going to start – try the operation again.
sentences.zh: 然后到了25日，也就是星期天，撒切尔夫人正在契克斯庄园，她得到了消息，他们要开始——再次尝试这次行动。

sentences.en: This time, it all goes absolutely splendidly.
sentences.zh: 这一次，一切都进行得绝对完美。

sentences.en: They attack an Argentine submarine, which is at South Georgia called the Santa Fe, and they cripple it.
sentences.zh: 他们袭击了停在南乔治亚岛的一艘阿根廷潜水艇“圣达菲”号，并将其重创。

sentences.en: The British commandos kind of arrive.
sentences.zh: 英国突击队员随之登陆。

sentences.en: The Argentines don't even fire a shot.
sentences.zh: 阿根廷人甚至没有开一枪。

sentences.en: They just basically give up completely straight away.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上直接就完全投降了。

sentences.en: The scrap metal – So are they conscripts?
sentences.zh: 废旧金属——所以他们是义务兵吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们是。

sentences.en: I mean, almost all the Argentines – I mean, there are obviously some professional troops, but a large proportion of their troops in the Argentine army are conscripts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几乎所有的阿根廷人——我的意思是，显然有一些职业军人，但阿根廷陆军中很大一部分士兵都是义务兵。

sentences.en: Because if you're a conscript, you wouldn't want to take on the SAS, would you?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是个义务兵，你才不想去跟特种空勤团硬碰硬，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I mean, in a snowstorm.
sentences.zh: 没错，我的意思是，还在暴风雪中。

sentences.en: These are very young guys.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常年轻的小伙子。

sentences.en: I mean, boys, basically, from Buenos Aires, who are in this freezing place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上就是来自布宜诺斯艾利斯的孩子，却被丢在这个冰天雪地的地方。

sentences.en: They've no idea where they are.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道自己身在何处。

sentences.en: Bloody awful.
sentences.zh: 真是糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: There's a load of scrap metal dealers.
sentences.zh: 这里有一堆废旧金属商。

sentences.en: It's only the SAS pitch up.
sentences.zh: 结果只有特种空勤团出现了。

sentences.en: So they surrender.
sentences.zh: 所以他们投降了。

sentences.en: And so that night, there is this incredibly dramatic moment.
sentences.zh: 于是在那天晚上，发生了这个极其戏剧性的时刻。

sentences.en: Are you going to give us a rendition of that, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你要给我们表演一段吗？

sentences.en: Or is that –
sentences.zh: 还是说——

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会。

sentences.en: I think we're going to stop at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想我们就在这里停下来。

sentences.en: Oh, no, that is a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，这真是个悬念。

sentences.en: So that's a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个悬念。

sentences.en: A lot of people won't be able to sleep.
sentences.zh: 很多人都会彻夜难眠。

sentences.en: They won't be able to sleep with excitement.
sentences.zh: 他们会兴奋得睡不着觉。

sentences.en: Well, in that case, they'll have to join the members club, won't they?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那样的话，他们就得加入会员俱乐部了，对吧？

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: The rest is historypod.com.
sentences.zh: The rest is historypod.com.

sentences.en: We will kick off with my sensational impression of Mrs. Thatcher's response to the triumph at South Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我们将以我对撒切尔夫人对南乔治亚岛大捷反应的精彩模仿作为开场。

sentences.en: And then we will look at the task force moving in the Falklands, the sinking of the Belgrano, the sinking of HMS Sheffield, the press reaction in Britain, which is extraordinary,
sentences.zh: 然后我们将探讨特混舰队进驻福克兰群岛、“贝尔格拉诺号”的击沉、“谢菲尔德”号驱逐舰的击沉、英国媒体不同寻常的反应，

sentences.en: and then how Britain ends up taking the Falklands back.
sentences.zh: 以及英国最终如何收复福克兰群岛。

sentences.en: Hasta luego.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。
